label: living library
html:
Living Library and research

Find the moment. Cite the source.

  • Smarter search

    Search no longer needs every word to match, so plain questions find the right source. Choose Exact words when you need every word. Optional semantic search finds similar meaning and runs on your computer after you turn it on in Settings.

  • Clip search + evidence cards

    Search inside videos for timestamped, deep-linked excerpts your AI can quote and cite. Now on everyday stdio MCP.

  • Standing capture

    Follow a YouTube channel, YouTube playlist, or podcast RSS feed. With capture enabled, new uploads and episodes land in your library.

  • Library reach over MCP

    Search the library, read items, and use resource templates and prompts from your MCP client.

  • Cited range export

    Quote a stretch of video or an episode with speaker labels, chapters, and provenance.

  • Chapter navigation

    Jump between chapters on items that have them.

  • Library, Reader, and Activity

    Search or paste a link in Library, open a capture in Reader, and follow Activity’s five-step strip. One Settings page saves individual preferences as you change them; the extension popup and setup keep capture and connection controls close.

  • Five research playbooks

    Use your own library for outlier posts, transcript intelligence, comment mining, creator teardowns, and repurposing. MCP agents can request cited packets without a model call. Optional ScrapeCreators discovery is off by default, with a default 25-credit daily cap and paid calls only with consent.

  • Podcasts and quieter notifications

    Podcast transcripts enter the searchable library; interrupted jobs resume after a restart. Feed audio stays off until you enable Auto-ingest. Captures show a toast instead of opening Explorer, and notifications can be muted or suppressed during fullscreen use.

  • More reliable YouTube capture

    Caption rate limits no longer fail the whole capture. Local transcription can fill in when an already-downloaded model is available; missing transcripts stay labeled. Requests are paced, yt-dlp is newer, and Activity distinguishes waiting, failure, and cancellation.

  • Tighter local boundaries

    Extension token minting checks the pinned extension ID, and page scripts cannot trigger capture buttons. Public-network checks protect supported fetch paths; error responses scrub paths and credentials, and corpus imports stay inside the exports folder.

label: corpus anatomy
html:
what you get per uoink

Why paste a transcript when you can feed the entire corpus?

Transcript-only tools flatten video into text. Uoink keeps the parts that make video useful: the words, the frames, the audience reaction, the channel context, and the source metadata.

  1. 01

    Capture the source.

    Transcript with timestamps, screenshots, description, title, thumbnail, channel context, and comments in one markdown file.

    See the workflow ->
  2. 02

    Keep the asset.

    Every capture writes to disk and into a local SQLite index. Search it later, cite it later, move it into your own vault.

    Browse features ->
  3. 03

    Hand it to AI.

    Paste transcript and frames into Claude or ChatGPT, or let an MCP agent search and cite your library.

    Open developer docs ->

label: local first
html:
local-first, by design

No account. No Uoink cloud. Your disk.

The helper runs on localhost. Your corpus lands on your disk. Entity extraction is opt-in and off by default. If you add your own Anthropic key, the model-usage meter shows real usage.

Read privacy ->

label: three audiences
html:
three doors, one corpus

Creators and developers use the same source card.

The card stays the shared object. The next move changes by job.

  • Creators.

    Find the moment you need, read the transcript beside the frames, and export a cited range for your next draft.

    See creator workflow ->

  • Developers.

    Give Claude Desktop or Cursor a local library to search and cite. Start with the stdio config or the Claude Desktop bundle.

    Open developer docs ->

  • Sources.

    Capture YouTube, X video and post text, podcasts, web articles, and Reddit threads into one local library.

install Uoink

One helper. One extension. Then the U button.

Download the helper, install the extension, open a video, and click Uoink. The helper bundles Python, yt-dlp, and ffmpeg so you never install them yourself.
